narrative.overview: VibeBreak behaves like a small part of macOS rather than a branded dashboard. State, configuration, testing, and recovery remain visible without decorative content.
keyCharacteristics: Native controls and familiar macOS terminology.
Restrained density with one clear task per section.
Semantic status communicated by text and color together.
No custom chrome, illustration, or marketing surface inside the app.

rules.name: The Semantic Color Rule
rules.body: Never replace system semantic colors with fixed values.

rules.name: The Utility Type Rule
rules.body: Do not introduce display typography or decorative monospace.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: A control receives depth only from its standard macOS state.

dos: Do use standard SwiftUI and AppKit controls before creating a custom one.
Do keep start and completion choices visible on the same settings tab.
Do expose source failures and incompatible schemas without guessing.
Do pair every semantic color with text or an icon label.
Do test long app names and missing applications.
donts: Don't turn settings sections into nested custom cards.
Don't add productivity scores, engagement metrics, or decorative charts.
Don't use hidden keyword fallbacks for agent lifecycle detection.
Don't disable native focus, contrast, or keyboard behavior for styling.
Don't claim a source is connected unless its schema gate has passed.
